assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's one curated REVIEWED item at basis_commit, read end to end with its front matter: series/konosuba/05 Specialist Synthesis/KONOSUBA_YUNYUN_CHARACTER_MONOGRAPH.md (19,610 bytes; status active_provisional, empty supersession arrays, do_not_use_as_current_authority false; generation SECONDARY_YUNYUN_EXPANDED_V1), a portrait of Yunyun across the Explosions (EXP01-03), Continued Explosions (CONTEXP01-02) and main (MAIN03-17) light novels, located by unit and paragraph or image page. Its declared boundary is the accepted MAIN17 principal histories and completed supplemental analysis, with 1,050 rechecked paragraph slots in twelve native units and twenty native EXP03 image pages; the monograph says these are overlapping joins to existing episodes, not independent observations, a second whole-source pass or held-out validation. Megumin narrates most Explosions material and Kazuma most main material; Yunyun's own focalization is limited to the four EXP03 image interludes and MAIN14 I13, and the portrait keeps narrator interpretation attributed. The linked reconstruction model and evidence index are not curated on this subject; no claim rests on them, and the monograph's own scoped Tier3 label was not adopted as a grade. Every claim inherits the active_provisional label. No primary source was inspected for this assessment.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Publication order, in-world order and analyst exposure are kept apart, as the monograph requires. States used: school and early travel before the established main-party relationship (EXP01 U043, EXP02 U044, EXP03 interludes, where she holds the Archwizard class while reporting only intermediate spells); advanced magic in her public self-description (MAIN03); Teleport provider and backup combatant (MAIN09, MAIN13); the chief trial, which changes her account of the chiefdom aspiration and ends with her selected as next chief while her father remains chief (MAIN14 I13, C4); Invisibility and the crime question (MAIN15); the temporary rescue agreement and refusal of permanent party membership (MAIN16); finite group transfers (MAIN17). Chronology splits at MAIN14: before it the chiefdom is the expected childhood goal she cannot justify; after it she wants to earn it and also admits friends in Axel would have led her to abandon it. Repertoire, level, mana reserve and registrations are never copied backward from MAIN17. The MAIN09-17 excluded components and dispersed Dust and Mask material are outside the boundary.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution) and the owner's A/B boundary direction of 24 November 2026 in PR #694, not yet recorded in the policy: A turns on the integration, individuation and transferability of the model within a declared scope; interpretations that predict the same behavior may coexist; divergent transfer conditions, missing evidence and unsettled dispositions are named and excluded rather than counted against the tier; held-out validation, analytical derivation, relationship labels and preserved source chronology are not barriers. Evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph gives a discriminating account built from wanted affiliation, selective inhibition, comparative self-appraisal and recognizably valued work, and says what changes the response. A named, useful, temporary role recruits her (MAIN16 C1 P190-210: agreement to Aqua's rescue after Dust names the task); a permanent institutional tie does not follow (the same scene: refusal of Mitsurugi's party). A specific known cost defeats a wanted invitation (EXP03 IMG032-039: the Alcanretia trip refused with gratitude and regret; MAIN03 C2 P574-605: Kazuma's walk refused when Megumin is present and her rival purpose is invoked). Information timing changes the outcome (CONTEXP02 U016 P188-220,259-266: she stays after learning the withheld destination in transit). Being singled out as needed overrides a voiced moral objection (MAIN15 C2 P217-260; MAIN09 F P268-321), which predicts her mistakes as well as her refusals. Not A: the ranking of company, recognition, self-chosen achievement and the particular rival is explicitly unsettled for irreversible conflicts (MAIN14 C4 P638-681), praise sensitivity is weakly supported and comparative self-appraisal is a LOW-confidence hypothesis (EXP02 U044 P583-640). Not C: the account does not stop at interpretation; it states the conditions that switch acceptance to refusal and objection to assistance, and where that stops.

Located state changes with triggers: early substantial but intermediate-level magic with real exhaustion (EXP01 U043 P239-365); a narrow chiefdom aspiration that MAIN14 I13 P8-47,73-83 turns into something she wants to earn, through Megumin's example; selection as next chief (C4 P6-20,54); later Axel residence and further achievement (C4 P638-681); finite logistics at MAIN17 F P730-760. The monograph says childhood awkwardness does not simply vanish with level gains. Not B: there is no volume-by-volume state ledger, and MAIN09-17 excluded components remain open, so states between the located points are not established. Not D: the MAIN14 change and the capacity growth are located and explained, not merely listed.

A relational register system in written Japanese: with Kazuma, さん, polite forms, hesitations and soft preliminary questions that can precede emphatic agreement or a concrete limit; with Megumin, plain forms, direct correction, accusation and rival declarations; reflective 私 in her own focalization; the chief introduction as a deliberate cultural register. The monograph adds use rules: a difficult request taking several starts, a firm no without becoming another person, technical knowledge and anger shortening speech, no scattered catchphrases. Not B: no counted forms or line-level locators for most patterns, and the monograph states these are written pragmatics, not audio or a measured stutter ratio. Not D: register is conditioned on the interlocutor and the act, not a list of tics.

Located ordinary items: food purchase and enjoyment, a wanted plush, treasured equipment from a shared shopping trip, paid or unpaid work for Vanir with tea and friend address (CONTEXP02 U016), training, travel, waiting, gifts, fatigue and a wish to share a festival. The monograph says these are narrower than a domestic preference inventory and that no favorite meal, budget rule or sleep schedule is established. Not C: apart from invitation choices, which are graded under relationships, there is no conditional account of ordinary choices. Not E: the items recur across several sources and are tied to relationships.

Directed differences with mechanisms: Megumin as particular friend, admired rival and source of humiliation and support, with a contact script of challenge, protest, protection and apology that does not license privacy violations or appropriation; Kazuma with deferential address, hesitant moral questions and strong responsiveness to being singled out as needed (MAIN15); Dust recognizing a useful role without licensing his pulling or insults (MAIN16); Iris, where protective promises stay promises and royal identity is not known early (CONTEXP01 U013 P104-153,389-424; CONTEXP02 U013 P150-178); Vanir, where being useful is rewarded without her recognizing exploitation; Aigis, with his own goals, refused proposals and failed and revised cooperation (MAIN14 I13 P49-85); Axis actors attributed individually. Not A: the reasons for refusing Mitsurugi are not settled, and Kazuma's flattering narration is not evidence of romance. Not C: each relationship states what that partner's conduct changes in hers.

Her own focalization is analysed in the four linked EXP03 image interludes (twenty native pages: approaches, misread signals, wanting a method for making friends) and MAIN14 I13 (the chiefdom aspiration, gratitude, admiration and competitive resolve). Elsewhere Megumin's and Kazuma's interpretations are kept attributed, and the monograph says no narrator's pity or joke measures her private motives. Not B: own-focalized material is confined to two loci, and her interior in the main-series scenes is reached through others. Not D: real first-person interior evidence is analysed for competing goals.

Located conduct with conditions: independent costly protection while Megumin hesitates (EXP01 U043 P239-365,515-580); unilateral Sleep on Megumin to protect her, without agreed consent (EXP03 U034 P168-240); hazardous anger with Light of Saber at Zesta's balloon (CONTEXP02 U018 P378-419); a failed Inferno inside Aigis followed by distraction at the word best friend (MAIN14 I13 P49-85); explicit capacity limits and coordination (MAIN17 F P730-760). The model predicts overreach as well as protection. Not B: the monograph's own exercise record says protective action does not identify a method over refusal, and no threshold for dangerous retaliation is given, so which response a new threat draws is not discriminated. Not D: the conflict responses are explained by information, resources and relationship, with located mistakes.

A located pattern: she objects that the MAIN09 campaign resembles the Demon Army yet keeps providing withdrawals (MAIN09 F P268-321); she raises a crime concern, then agrees emphatically once Kazuma calls her his uniquely necessary friend, and her Invisibility enables the coercive plan (MAIN15 C2 P217-260); the Sleep decision overrides Megumin's consent for protection (EXP03 U034). The monograph rejects both general pacifism and an infallible moral veto. Not B: what would make her objection hold against an affiliation appeal is never shown, and her knowledge of later details in MAIN15 is limited. Not D: the objection-then-assistance mechanism is located twice and predicts a characteristic error.

Located comic patterns: recruitment failure, peer teasing, theatrical chief introductions and attention captured by a friendship word, with the monograph's transfer rule (reduce physical exaggeration and repeated public humiliation, keep goals, resistance and errors). Her own enacted play is mostly the theatrical introduction and the rival-challenge script with Megumin. Not C: there is no account of when she jokes or plays and what stops it; most of the comedy is built around her. Not E: the patterns recur across sources and have a stated transfer rule.

Dedicated coverage across three series lines with unit and paragraph locators, accepted whole-source histories and 1,050 rechecked native slots plus twenty image pages, with each narrator's access kept separate. Not B: the item is active_provisional, the larger secondary census and the MAIN09-17 excluded components are open, some Dust and Mask material is derivative or lead-level only, and the linked model is not curated here. Not D: one dedicated item covers the main arcs and their limits with locators.

Affirmative located limits: refusals that defeat a will-do-anything-for-a-friend rule (EXP03 IMG032-039; MAIN03 C2 P574-605; MAIN16 C1 P190-210); the MAIN15 attribution correction (she casts Invisibility; the ice on the hut is Kazuma's; Silent is named but not shown cast); the failed Inferno (MAIN14 I13 P49-85); staying in Alcanretia does not supply earlier informed assent (CONTEXP02 U016); Megumin's narration does not establish whether the EXP01 dagger hit was aimed; Kazuma's narration does not establish romance; Aigis's protection is not deleted from the trial success (I13 P3-6). Not A: several are attribution bounds rather than contradictions of a model claim. Not C: these are evidenced bounds, not silence.

Three clocks are kept apart, an interlude's local stage is not equated with surrounding chapters, and capacities are not copied backward from MAIN17; the EXP03 guild episode's class-versus-spell state is located. Not B: there is no dated in-world chronology across the main volumes, and states between located points are open. Not D: the ordering rules and the MAIN14 split are explicit.

conditions: Illustrative written-Japanese-derived lines only, never presented as quotation.

With Kazuma: さん, polite forms, hesitations and soft preliminary questions that can end in emphatic agreement or a concrete limit. With Megumin: plain forms, correction, accusation and rival declarations. Own reflection: 私.
A difficult request may take several starts; a refusal stays firm without changing her into another person; technical knowledge and urgent anger may shorten or sharpen the speech.
No catchphrase scattering, measured stutter or audio performance is implied; translation adapts address and endings functionally.
scenario_readiness.note: The register system constrains short lines enough for illustrative use in the sampled relationships. Not READY: written pragmatics without counted forms or audio. Not NOT_READY: register is conditioned on interlocutor and act with explicit use rules.

conditions: State her chronology (before or after the MAIN14 trial), her repertoire and mana at that point, what she knows about the destination or task, and whether the offer is temporary and role-specific or permanent.
Predict acceptance of a named, useful, temporary role and refusal of a permanent institutional tie or a destination with a specific known cost; give alternatives where the monograph gives no decider.
When Kazuma or a comparable valued companion singles her out as necessary, predict a voiced objection followed by possible assistance with a harmful plan; do not predict an infallible veto.
Transfer to a comparable but unsampled companion is a separate, lower-confidence condition.
Exclude irreversible choices between company and achievement or chiefdom, and any romance outcome.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: After the MAIN14 chief trial and selection as next chief, living in Axel, with MAIN15-17 capacities as located; an earlier state only when the scenario names it and uses only the repertoire established for it.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Megumin as particular friend and rival, Kazuma as a valued companion who can single her out as needed, or a stranger or acquaintance offering company, a task or a party place; any other partner is a lower-confidence transfer.
setting_constraints: Canonical-comic Axel-area adventuring or social life with actual magic and finite mana.
Realistic transfer only with reduced physical exaggeration and public humiliation, no imported magic or level, and goals, resistance and errors preserved.
No romance content and no irreversible company-versus-achievement decision.

scenario_readiness.note: The affiliation, invitation-cost and singled-out-as-needed conditions support bounded prediction of acceptance, refusal and voiced objection in comparable situations. Not READY: the achievement-company ranking is unsettled for irreversible choices, and the conditions are sampled from a limited set of partners. Not NOT_READY: each condition is located and states what would change the response.

conditions: Outings, invitations, shared purchases, tea and work with the sampled partners (Megumin, Kazuma, Vanir, Iris and strangers as in EXP03).
No invented favorite meal, budget rule, sleep schedule or universal taste in entertainment.
scenario_readiness.note: Invitations, outings, tea, gifts, food and work for others are sampled with stated reasons for acceptance and refusal. Not READY: no domestic preference inventory. Not NOT_READY: the invitation conditions are located across several sources.

conditions: Predict a hesitant moral question or objection, then possible assistance when singled out as necessary; do not predict principled weighing to a settled verdict.
Protective action may be unilateral and may override consent, as with Sleep in EXP03 U034.
Her knowledge of later details in a plan must be stated, not assumed.
scenario_readiness.note: Supports predicting that she voices concern and can then assist under an affiliation appeal, and that she can override a friend's consent to protect them. Not READY: no case shows what makes her objection hold. Not NOT_READY: the pattern is located twice with its mechanism.
The monograph says Kazuma's flattering private narrative is not proof of romance and asks the model to keep warm gratitude without romance; nothing in the item establishes romantic conduct.

conditions: Adventuring and support work with finite, stated capacity; she reports limits and coordinates others rather than acting as an unlimited transport device.
Equipment or information gaps may block her expertise, as with the MAIN14 Inferno inside Aigis.
As next chief she is not the chief; no institutional duties beyond those located.
scenario_readiness.note: Adventuring roles are well located: Teleport provider and backup combatant (MAIN09 F P199-226), escape planning (MAIN13 C4 P283-295), scouting and intermediate-spell economy (MAIN14 I13), transfer counts and coordination (MAIN17 F P730-760), and selection as next chief. Not READY: exact level, reserves and the chief's duties are not established. Not NOT_READY: roles, limits and coordination are located.

known_limits.statement: Company, recognition, self-chosen achievement and the particular rival are not ranked for irreversible conflicts; MAIN14 C4 P638-681 shows she wants to earn the chiefdom and also that friends in Axel would have led her to abandon it.
Inaccurate comparative self-valuation is a LOW-confidence hypothesis from one concentrated sequence (EXP02 U044 P583-640), not a diagnosis of permanent low self-esteem.
Most scenes are narrated by Megumin or Kazuma; their pity, jokes, remembered invitations and appraisals are not measurements of her private motives.
In MAIN15 she casts Invisibility; the ice on the hut is Kazuma's, and Silent is named as the next task without a shown cast.
Repertoire, level, mana reserve, Teleport registrations and responsibilities cannot be copied backward from MAIN17 to earlier states.
Kazuma's flattering narration and his gift and invitations do not establish romance.

Eight paired synthetic contrasts with sixteen same-author responses expose weaknesses (protective method versus refusal, weak praise sensitivity, an unresolved irreversible tradeoff) and are not source events, independent review or an accuracy score.
The larger secondary census, the MAIN09-17 excluded components and dispersed Dust and Mask material are outside the item's evidence; behavior there is not assessed.
The linked reconstruction model and evidence index are not curated on this subject, so no rule-level claim from them is used.
